The induced effect opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it. In this specific switch-on situation the solenoid field/flux is increasing, so the induced field is opposite to the solenoid field as a consequence of opposing that increase. If a student says only that the induced field 'opposes the original field', treat this as overgeneralised/incomplete and refine the principle rather than affirming it as generally correct.
